_comment: Per-crate Rust line-coverage floors. Read by scripts/verify-coverage-floors.py. See done-todo-codebase-reliability.md P1-2 for why the figure is a ratchet rather than a target.

_measured.command: cargo llvm-cov --workspace --all-features --exclude kasirmu-app --exclude kasirmu-mobile --exclude kasirmu-bridge --json --output-path coverage-probe.json
_measured.note: kasirmu-bridge was excluded because an unrelated uncommitted change in another session had one of its tests failing, and cargo llvm-cov aborts on any failing test. The four crates below are the ones P1-2 names, and none of them is bridge.

_policy: Each floor sits 2 percentage points BELOW the measured value. A ratchet, not a target: it freezes the level reached so a regression fires, without demanding work nobody has agreed to fund. platform-sync is deliberately the lowest floor because it IS the lowest coverage (68.7%), and it is also the crate this checklist calls the highest-risk surface -- the floors are not uniform because the crates are not.
_moving_a_floor: Lowering a floor is the failure this gate exists to catch, so it must be a deliberate, recorded act: change the number here, update _measured with a fresh date and command, and say in the commit message which crate regressed and why the loss is acceptable. Raising a floor is encouraged and needs no justification beyond the measurement.

_measured_ui.command: cd ui && npm run test:coverage  (vitest v8 -> coverage/ui/coverage-summary.json)
_measured_ui.stability: Two consecutive runs on 2026-10-28 produced identical percentages in all four metrics (delta 0.00), so a two-point floor cannot fire on run-to-run noise.
_measured_ui.supersedes: docs/records/benchmarks/coverage-report-2026-07-20.md set Lines >= 50%, Branches >= 40%, Functions >= 50%. Nothing enforced them and the code has since reached 85.65 / 75.77 / 79.29, so those numbers could never fire. They are replaced by this ratchet, not merely raised.

_policy_ui: Same ratchet rule as the Rust floors: each floor sits 2 percentage points BELOW the measured value, so it freezes the level reached and fires on a regression without demanding work nobody has funded. Raised only by re-measuring; lowering is a deliberate, recorded act.
